title: Micro Onramp: Seller Heuristics Lab (Draft)
body:
Purpose
---
Quick, tactical heuristics and sample scripts for SEs and sellers running short pilot engagements where customers care about latency, cost, and predictable rollouts. This is intentionally compact (one-pager + short appendices) so reps can use it live during calls.

Context / problem we solve
- Many pilot conversations stall because engineering leads worry about unpredictable token costs and degraded tail latency.
- Field needs a tiny, shareable playbook that: 1) qualifies risk fast, 2) prescribes 1–2 low-friction mitigations, 3) gives a fallback script for procurement/security pushback.

How to use this doc (seller flow)
1) Open with 30s anchor: "Most teams we work with get a predictable latency and cost profile within the first two pilot sprints by pinning a model family + a canary fallback policy."
2) Use the qualifying checklist (below) on the call to decide: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
3) Pick one recommended mitigation (cache / quantize / batch) and offer a clear next step (demo + conservative estimate).

Qualifying checklist (ask these on discovery)
- Expected peak qps during pilot? (estimate: <50qps, 50–500qps, >500qps)
- Typical request length (tokens): short (<64), medium (64–512), long (>512)
- Does customer need VPC or data isolation for pilot? (yes/no)
- Success metric for pilot: latency SLO, cost per 1k tokens, or quality retention?
- Is there an internal procurement SLA/approval that requires a committed spend? (yes/no)

Decision heuristics (one-line rules)
- If peak <50qps and no strict isolation -> Hosted API + KV prefix caching. Rationale: fastest time-to-value, low ops.
- If qps 50–500 but latencies matter -> Dedicated with small reserved pool + autoscale buffer. Rationale: predictable tail latency.
- If VPC/air-gap required or enterprise procurement -> Private deployment trial (small node set). Rationale: compliance and audit controls.
- If >500qps or sustained heavy throughput -> propose Dedicated commit with throughput tiers. Note: include burst policy.

Recommended single mitigations (pick one)
- Caching-first: Enable prefix/KV cache for repeat calls (chat context reuse). Impact: reduces tokens and latency for repeated flows.
- Conservative quantization: Use an FP16->int8 profile for non-critical generation to halve GPU memory and reduce unit cost. Impact: ~1.5–2x throughput improvement in many models.
- Aggressive batching: Use micro-batching with target latency budget (e.g., batch window 10–30ms) for throughput-heavy cases. Impact: reduces per-token cost but adds small queuing latency.

Sample scripts (swap in customer details)
- If worried about cost: "Totally fair — a common pattern is we start the pilot on Hosted with KV caching turned on and a fixed token budget for the demo week. That keeps your spend predictable and we share a live dashboard so you can see token usage in real time."
- If worried about latency: "We can reserve a small Dedicated pool for the pilot and configure a canary fallback to a lower-cost model for non-critical requests. That keeps tail latency tight while we validate quality."
- If procurement asks for private hosting: "We offer a turnkey Private deployment for pilots — minimal infra footprint (1–2 small nodes) with a private control plane and KMS integration to meet audit needs."

Canary / fallback mini-checklist (on-handoff to solutions engineer)
- Define primary model and 1 fallback (compatible tokenizer/arch).
- Set fallback policy: on 95th percentile latency breach OR error rate >1% -> route to fallback.
- Measure quality delta on a small eval set (10–20 prompts) before enabling fallback in production.
- Create a cost cap alert (daily) for pilot token consumption.

Objection rebuttals (short)
- "We can’t predict costs": "We’ll start with a capped token budget and a live dashboard — if usage spikes we throttle to preserve budget while we triage."
- "We don’t want to commit to Dedicated yet": "Treat Dedicated as a short-term pilot commit (30–60 days) with rollback to Hosted if volume doesn’t materialize."
- "Quantization hurts quality": "We recommend A/B’ing quantized and non-quantized variants on a targeted eval set; often quality impact is negligible for retrieval- or summarization-heavy flows."

Appendix A — Example pilot plan (two-week sprint)
Week 0: kickoff, finalize telemetry and evaluation prompts, set token budget.
Week 1: deploy on Hosted with KV caching; collect latency + token metrics; run eval set.
Week 2: if stable and throughput justifies, propose Dedicated trial (1 GPU pool) and show cost delta. Decision checkpoint at end of week 2.

Appendix B — Quick metrics to capture (dashboard pointers)
- 50/95/99 latency quantiles, tokens per request, token spend per route, error rate, model fallback count.

Open questions / TODOs (workshopping)
- Add one-liner architecture diagrams (hosted vs dedicated vs private) — draw in next iteration.
- Need productized scripts for enabling per-route caching from Console (ticket: JIRA-3722).
- Create a 30s demo video for sellers showing dashboard and token cap flow. Owner: Marisol.

Notes to self
- Keep this intentionally short — convert to two-slide cheat sheet + single-page battlecard for reps.
- Prefer live links to pilot templates in the repo rather than embedding long config snippets here.
